readme:
# Pathfinder — a 42 mm hobby rocket, built with LabWired and kernelCAD

Pathfinder is an original 0.8 m hobby rocket for a 24 mm F-class motor. It has an STM32F411 flight computer, barometric apogee deployment of a 450 mm parachute, an arm switch on the airframe and a side-mounted action camera. One chain connects every part of the design:

**CAD masses → stability and flight physics → sensor stimuli → firmware on the twin → verified requirements → routed PCB.**

## Run it

Open **Model** and press **Run**. The saved stimulus track flies the twin through the full flight. The serial console shows:

```
SELFTEST baro=1 imu=1 → PHASE PAD_SAFE → GROUND_PA=99892 → CAMERA_POWER_ON → CAMERA_REC_START
LAUNCH t_ms≈130 → BURNOUT t_ms≈2100 → APOGEE_DETECTED / DEPLOY t_ms≈9450 → PYRO_OFF
LANDED → CAMERA_REC_STOP → CAMERA_POWER_OFF → FLIGHT apogee_m=… → OUTPUTS_SAFE PYRO=0 CAM=0
```

## Verified on the twin (5 of 5 requirements, oracle proof)

| ID | Requirement |
|----|-------------|
| R1 | Barometer and IMU pass self-test. The pyro channel is off at reset. |
| R2 | The arm switch calibrates ground pressure, powers the camera and starts recording. |
| R3 | Launch is detected from axial g. Burnout is detected between T+1.9 s and T+2.3 s. |
| R4 | The pyro channel fires after true apogee and before T+10.0 s, then switches off after 1 s. |
| R5 | Landing is detected, the camera stops and powers off, the summary apogee is 355–372 m, all outputs end safe. |

## Physics

| Quantity | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Liftoff mass | 351 g (dry 288 g) | kernelCAD BOM, part densities |
| CG / CP | 320 mm / 213 mm above the aft end | BOM centroids / Barrowman (ogive nose, 3 fins) |
| Static margin | 2.55 cal at liftoff, 3.17 cal at burnout | |
| Apogee | 364 m at T+8.9 s | 1-D RK4, ISA atmosphere, Cd 0.55 |
| Max speed / accel | 86 m/s / 8.1 g | |
| Rail exit (1.5 m) | 15.0 m/s | |
| Descent under 450 mm chute | 4.7 m/s, landing T+86 s | Cd 1.5 |
| Fin, 30 N tip strike | 11.9 MPa, SF 3.3 on 40 MPa birch ply, 0.50 mm deflection | CalculiX FEA in kernelCAD |

The fin span was cut from 55 to 40 mm after the first mass budget gave 3.7 cal (over-stable).

## CAD

kernelCAD project `K_DmeiaD`, revision 2: https://app.kernelcad.com/p/K_DmeiaD?version=2
31 parts: ogive nose, payload and booster tubes, avionics coupler with switch band and static ports, bulkheads, sled, flight-computer PCB, 1S LiPo, parachute and shock cord, 3 fins, 24 mm motor mount, retainer, motor, camera pod and camera, rail buttons, launch rail. Mechanism check: real (3 prismatic joints, no collisions). The **flight animation** plays the simulated altitude (time ×10, altitude 1:200), then nose separation and parachute ejection at the firmware deploy time. In the Model view, the red arm key on the switch band drives the arm-switch input of the twin.

## PCB

Board `pcb_64aa5b709085de4d` rev 2: 30/30 nets routed (Freerouting), KiCad 9 DRC passed, gerbers, drill, BOM, positions and STEP exported.

## Boundary — read this

- **Flight clock.** The twin build runs the firmware's flight clock 60× faster (`TWIN_TIME_SCALE 60`). I2C/SPI traffic stays real-time. **Set `TWIN_TIME_SCALE` to 1 before you flash hardware.** The firmware prints a warning at boot when it is not 1.
- **Open loop.** The sensor track comes from the physics script, not from a plant stepped with the firmware. The 46-entry track (saved-stimuli limit is 64) samples the barometer every 0.5 s in ascent and 8 s under the chute.
- **Motor.** The thrust curve is a generic 24 mm F-class profile (39 N·s), not a certified motor file. Use your motor's `.eng` data.
- **PCB fit.** The routed board is 71 × 97 mm. The sled in a 38.4 mm coupler takes about 32 mm. The board is an electrical study; a narrow outline is needed before fabrication.
- **Stand-ins.** Battery = barrel-jack supply part, camera = 4-pin header, e-match = 1.5 Ω resistor, MOSFETs use TO-92 footprints. No power switch in the netlist (it sits in the battery negative lead).
- **microSD** logging is in the firmware but the twin's SD model does not complete init, so `SD_FAIL` is expected in the twin.
- Nothing here was flown. Model verification is not flight certification. Follow your national rocketry code and the motor maker's limits.
